tender.title: NHS South Yorkshire  ICB Barnsley -  Health provision for children and young people with special education needs and disabilities at Greenacre School
tender.description: The ICB requires Apollo Healthcare to deliver health provision for children and young people with special education needs and disabilities at Greenacre Special School.  The provider is required to provide efficient health provision through a skilled workforce made up of Specialist Nurses and Healthcare Assistants. The workforce will work collaboratively with school staff and NHS clinical staff including occupational therapists, speech and language therapist, learning disability nurses, epilepsy and diabetes teams and any other professionals required to support the delivery of health care provision into Greenacre School.

lots.description:
NHS South Yorkshire Integrated Care Board are intending to award a contract to the existing provider following direct award process C of the Provider Selection Regime.

The approximate lifetime value of the contract is £953,938. The contract will be awarded for three years The contract will be awarded to :

Apollo Care, Unit 12 Stonecross House, Doncaster Road, Kirk Sandall, Doncaster, DN3 1QS

The award has been made using the following criteria:

Key criteria 1. Quality and innovation - Weighting (20%)

The ICB predicts that Apollo Healthcare will continue to deliver health provision into Greenacre School and to support pupils with complex medical conditions.

Apollo Healthcare is expected to continue to maintain their well established collaborative working relationship with Greenacre, the ICB, local authority commissioners and NHS clinical workforce, ensuring that every pupil with a medical condition is properly supported so that they have full access to education. Apollo Healthcare will continue to provide appropriately trained staff who contribute to the delivery of health care planning and support pupils in achieving their identified goals and outcomes.

The ICB expects the provider to maintain high standards of quality and safety, continue effective governance arrangements and work collaboratively with commissioners and partners to identify opportunities for further service improvements.

Given Apollo Healthcare’s established understanding of the new clinical intervention model and have been fundamental in the planning process, have existing workforce arrangements and positive delivery history, the ICB considers Apollo Healthcare to be well placed to continue delivering the requirements of the service.

Key criteria 2. Value - Weighting (20%)

The ICB expects Apollo Healthcare to continue delivering healthcare provision at Greenacre School in accordance with the agreed contractual arrangements, ensuring the effective use of resources and the delivery of value for money. The provider will continue to support pupils with complex medical needs through robust healthcare planning and by working collaboratively with Greenacre School, NHS clinicians, and local commissioners to optimise outcomes for pupils.

The ICB expects Apollo Healthcare to maintain an appropriate balance between cost, quality, and outcomes, ensuring that financial efficiency is achieved without compromising the quality, safety, or effectiveness of care. Through this approach, the provider will continue to deliver a high-quality, sustainable service that meets the needs of pupils while supporting the strategic objectives of the wider health and care system.

Key criteria 3. Integration, collaboration and service sustainability - Weighting (20%)

The ICB expect Apollo Healthcare to continue operating as an integrated partner of health care delivery and provision in Greenacre School. This is consistent with national guidance from DfE for Supporting pupils at school with medical conditions and guidance from Royal College of Nursing for meeting health needs in educational other community settings.

Apollo Healthcare will continue to work collaboratively with Greenacre school staff, BHFNT and NHS clinical teams, the ICB, local authority commissioners and other partners to ensure effective delivery of healthcare provision.

Apollo Healthcare is expected to maintain an established multidisciplinary approach, support service resilience and contribute to the ongoing sustainability of health care provision and clinical intervention at Greenacre School. Maintaining continuity with the current provider will ensure that existing relationships, processes and workforce arrangements continue without disruption"

Key criteria 4. Improving access, reducing health inequalities and facilitating choice - (20%)

The ICB expects Apollo Healthcare to continue providing accessible, person-centred health care provision for pupils with complex medical needs. Apollo Healthcare will continue to work collaboratively with school staff, the ICB, local authority commissioners and NHS clinicians to ensure pupils are allocated to the correct tier of support and that pupils can access and receive the support they need in their education setting. By having accessibility to the support and services they need, pupils will ultimately have improved health and wellbeing and health inequalities will be reduced.

Key criteria 5. Social value - Weighting (20%)

The ICB expects Apollo Healthcare to continue delivering social value throughout the contract by sustaining local employment opportunities, investing in workforce training, skills development, and career progression, and supporting collaborative partnership working across the local system. Apollo Healthcare will also be expected to contribute to local economic growth by utilising local suppliers and procuring equipment and resources locally wherever possible. In addition, the provider should support environmental sustainability through measures that reduce waste, increase recycling, and minimise energy consumption and carbon emissions.

Throughout the lifetime of the contract, Apollo Healthcare will continue to deliver high-quality healthcare provision and clinical interventions that improve outcomes for children and young people attending Greenacre School, as well as providing support to their families. The provider will be expected to maintain and strengthen its links with the local community by promoting opportunities for student placements, work experience, and workforce development initiatives. Apollo Healthcare will also continue to support activities and initiatives that strengthen community connections, promote social value, and enhance the experiences and outcomes of children and young people receiving healthcare services. Through these commitments, the provider will contribute to the wider social, economic, and environmental wellbeing of the Barnsley population alongside the delivery of its core service responsibilities.

tender.description:
The service is to deliver comprehensive, inclusive, and needs-led support for all People Living With or affected by HIV ("PLWH"), including those at increased risk of acquiring HIV, and those who support and care for them. 
Kirklees supports the ambitious and important national target to end new cases of HIV in England by 2030 - the service will contribute towards the achievement of this locally through the provision of both universal and suitably targeted prevention work. 
The service will use a holistic approach to focus on prevention and support PLWH to maximise health, well-being, quality of life and social integration, recognising the interdependencies between an effective support offer and the prevention of transmission and new cases of HIV.

lots.description:
Given significant improvements in prevention and declines in new cases, the government has made a commitment to end HIV transmissions in England by 2030. As recommended in the recent report from the HIV Commission reviewing progress towards this goal, achieving this will require a significant boost in prevention, testing, and early diagnosis, alongside an increased focus on tackling stigma, discrimination, and health inequalities within the health system.
The work of the HIV Support and Prevention Service will complement other (HIV specific and generic) health and social care services and enable people living with and affected by HIV in Kirklees to live independent lives, effectively manage their long-term condition, and enjoy good quality of life and health and wellbeing. It will also work to reduce (and ultimately eliminate) HIV transmission, reduce late diagnosis rates, and tackle HIV related stigma and discrimination.

The Service is designed to deliver intensive, proactive, and flexible community-based care for individuals with Serious Mental Illness (SMI) who present with elevated levels of complexity and risk and for whom engagement with traditional mental health services is a challenge.
Delivery will be through a blended model between Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust (NSFT) as the Head Provider and the Sub-Contractor, ensuring a comprehensive offer that integrates clinical expertise with community-based engagement and recovery support.
The Sub-Contractor will play a critical role in enabling engagement, promoting recovery, and addressing the wider determinants of health, working as a fully integrated partner alongside NSFT clinical teams.

No individual is excluded from care due to disengagement, complexity, or social circumstances.
Assertive Engagement and Outreach
The Sub-Contractor will:
• Deliver proactive, persistent outreach, particularly where individuals are disengaged
• Provide frequent contact, including daily visits in line with the care plan
• Engage individuals in a variety of settings, including:
- Their home
- Community settings
- Places where they feel safe
- In-reaching into hospitals or prisons if required to establish engagement and promote continuity of care
• Use creative and flexible engagement approaches, including:
- Doorstep engagement
- Accompaniment to appointments
- Informal relational contact
- Demonstrate the ability to sustain engagement over extended periods, particularly where trust is low
The sub-contractor(s) will provide:
• Assertive Engagement and Outreach
• Practical Support for Daily Living

• Support to Access Healthcare (Including Mental Health Care)
• Medication Support (Non-Clinical)

tender.title: CN220350 - Therapies: SEN, Adoption Support Service and VSK (previously SC21032)
tender.description:
SEN Therapies (Lot 1)
The Council recognises that SEN therapy service providers have an important role in improving a child or young person's (CYP's) participation in learning experiences and access to curriculum opportunities and outcomes for our children who have an Education, Health and Care (EHC) Plan. The Council aims to establish a relational contracting approach with providers on the Qualified Provider List (QPL) that will:
• recognise the interdependencies between local authorities, service providers, Ofsted and other stakeholders;
• facilitate co operation, shared learning and improvement;
• enable the Council to anticipate and respond quickly to the changing needs of CYP with an EHC plan;
• support joint working between the Council's education services and therapy service providers to help improve outcomes for CYP with an EHC plan;
• help ensure sufficiency and suitability of therapy provision tailored to the current and anticipated needs of CYP with an EHC plan; and
• ensure fairness in commercial arrangements between commissioners and providers, with transparency of prices.
Adoption Support Service (Lot 2)
The Adoption Support Fund (ASF) has been established to help adoptive families access the services they need more easily. The ASF provides funds to local authorities (LAs) and Regional Adoption Agencies (RAAs) to pay for essential therapeutic services for eligible adoptive families and families with a Special Guardianship Order (SGO). The aim of the ASF and the support it funds is to:
• improve outcomes for young people and families;
• improve the core adoption/SGO support offered to families; and
• build the evidence base so that interventions demonstrate their effectiveness and value for money.
Virtual Schools Kent (Lot 3)
Virtual School Head Teachers (VSHs) are responsible for promoting the educational achievement of children looked after by the local authority. For some young people, a therapeutic approach or intervention may be required to support access to, or
engagement with, education.
Kent Children in Care (CiC), aged 3 to 18, are supported by Virtual School Kent (VSK). Pupil Premium Plus (PP+), Post 16 Pupil Premium Plus (P16PP+), or Early Years Pupil Premium (EYPP) funding can be used to pay for activities that:
a) improve the learning targets in children's Personal Education Plans (PEPs); and
b) encourage CiC to be more involved in and interested in their education.

tender.title: North Staffordshire Combined Healthcare NHS Trust Out of Area Psychiatric Intensive Care (PICU) Placement
tender.description: Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit inpatient bed CPV: 85111500-5

lots.description:
This Contract Award Notice is placed under the Healthcare Services (Provider Selection Regime)Regulations 2023, Regulation 8 for Direct Award Process B, where the the Trust is awarding this contract having conducted spot purchasing analysis and concluded that this is the only available option.
The Trust has a choice of providers, and is not seeking to restrict the number of providers.
The service provided is Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) inpatient bed.  Psychiatric Intensive Care Units (PICU) are specialist wards that provide inpatient mental health care, assessment and comprehensive treatment to individuals who are experiencing the most acutely disturbed phase of a serious mental disorder.  The contract has been awarded following direct award process B. At  £1,081.00 per day for a nominal period of 4 weeks as the duration is unknown. The patient would be reviewed daily Mon-Fri and would be re-patriated where clinically appropriate. Estimated total cost £30,268 From 46284 to not known. 
The Trust had a spot purchasing arrangements with them in the past, and this is a continuation of that service for a new placement, now coming through the Trust whereas previously it sat under the ICB. 
The contract is new as the Trust are placing the contract directly but that the arrangements have been previously in place under spot purchasing via the ICB.
